(base section + all seven `extended_policies`, including every `overwrite`, every `prerequisite` and
every declared factor's full ladder) against the 68 published documents of

Corpus hash `80bdbebfece560d6e4d1a0e21a44cabd3f7caaa0b1b393d3a6024b6ffce0c28f`. The scan is not limited
to the branch task 0 hits; untriggered tiers and untriggered packages are covered.

**Entry conditions (checked and cited, not re-run).** The brief supplies the policy-side PASS verdict
for this difficulty after two rounds; the `check_docs.py` snapshot for product `rentals`
(`docs=68 roles={'factor': 35, 'facet': 9, 'baseline': 7, 'hub': 7, 'policy': 10}`, required

outstanding); and the `check_traceability.py` snapshot for `equipment_rental_desk`
(`0.json 24 copied / 0 missing`, `1.json 19 copied / 0 missing`, `TRACEABILITY OK`). The

### D. The five prerequisites, listed separately

Verified programmatically: each `policy_source` string appears **verbatim** in exactly one of the 68
documents, and that document is the hub of the policy it blocks.

| Blocked policy | Depends on | Form | Prerequisite sentence, verbatim | Carrying document (the only one) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rentals_ext_counter_settlement` | `rentals_ext_damage_assessment` | **state** | "The amount the guest is asked to hand over is fixed only after every finding a technician has entered against an item on the agreement carries the amount the guest bears for it." | `counter_settlement_of_a_rental_agreement_b9239ea0` |
| `rentals_ext_counter_settlement` | `rentals_ext_late_handin_fee` | **state** | "The amount the guest is asked to hand over is fixed only after the account carries the shop fee owed for the days the kit stayed out beyond the date written on the agreement." | `counter_settlement_of_a_rental_agreement_b9239ea0` |
| `rentals_ext_security_hold_settlement` | `rentals_ext_counter_settlement` | **state** | "What goes back to the guest is worked out only after the money collected against the agreement stands against the charges raised on it." | `security_hold_release_entry_c5b5470f` |
| `rentals_ext_extension_charge` | `rentals_ext_party_rate_charge` | **state** | "The charge for the extra days is fixed only after the hire rate for the days the agreement was written for stands on its rental account." | `rental_extension_entry_9c5075c2` |
| `rentals_ext_extension_charge` | `rentals_ext_model_change_fee` | **state** | "The charge for the extra days is fixed only after every change of model recorded on the agreement carries the shop's fee owed for it." | `rental_extension_entry_9c5075c2` |

**Ordering connective and strength.** Each sentence keeps "fixed only after" / "worked out only
after" exactly as the source writes it — a hard gate on when the figure is settled, neither softened
to advice nor hardened beyond the source. None is restated anywhere else, and **no depended-on
policy's document carries the blocked side's sentence**: `damage_finding_assessment_entry`,
`late_handin_fee_entry`, `counter_settlement_of_a_rental_agreement`, `hire_rate_charge_entry` and
`model_change_fee_entry` say nothing about who waits on them.

**Resolution basis, per edge** (the sentence + the depended-on documents + the records):

1. *counter ← assessment.* The state named is "every finding … carries the amount the guest bears for
   it". `damage_finding_assessment_entry_8b49d2bc` describes the write in the same words the records
   use: "A finding entered when kit was checked back in stands on the agreement's rental account at
   nil until it is assessed" and "Writing the figure onto the finding raises the amount still to be
   collected". The record is the `rentals_damage_charge` row carrying `amount_usd = 0.0`. Resolvable.
2. *counter ← late fee.* The state is "the account carries the shop fee owed for the days the kit
   stayed out beyond the date written on the agreement". `late_handin_fee_entry_7b29a43e`: "Kit …
   that reaches a shop counter after the date written on that agreement carries the shop's fee for
   the days it stayed out" and "One entry books a single late hand-in fee on the agreement's rental
   account". The records are `due_date` / `returned_date` and an account with no fee row. Resolvable.
3. *hold release ← counter.* The state is "the money collected against the agreement stands against
   the charges raised on it". `counter_settlement_of_a_rental_agreement_b9239ea0`: "One entry books a
   single payment … and lowers the amount still to be collected … that entry is what the account then
   carries as money collected against the agreement". The records are the charge rows and the single
   payment row leaving 65.00 USD. Resolvable.
4. *extension ← hire rate.* The state is "the hire rate for the days the agreement was written for
   stands on its rental account". `hire_rate_charge_entry_f7aaf673`: "this is the basis on which that
   rate is settled and put on the agreement's rental account"; "One entry books a single hire-rate
   entry … covering the days the agreement was written for". Resolvable.
5. *extension ← change fee.* The state is "every change of model recorded on the agreement carries
   the shop's fee owed for it". `model_change_fee_entry_06531b2f`: "A change of model or size already
   recorded on an agreement … carries the shop's fee for having made it"; "One entry books a single
   change-of-model fee on the agreement's rental account". Resolvable.

`condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect`, `gate` and `kind` appear in **no** document — checked by
searching the corpus for each tool name and for the `condition` strings.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 68 documents was traced to a source atom. The two checks this layer
exists for:

- **Cross-problem operational guidance:** none. No document tells the reader to "call X first", to
  "handle Y before Z", or names any other problem's tool, policy id or document. A regex sweep for
  routing language (`only after`, `must first`, `first raise/assess/settle/record/call`, `refer to`,
  `see the`, `step N`, `checklist`, `procedure`, `roadmap`, `in this order:`) returned exactly six
  hits, all of them the five prerequisite sentences on their own blocked side (the counter hub
  carrying two) — and one descriptive "the exception on every column" in the late-fee schedule, which
  is a comparison of the Season-Long Lease Package's figures with the rest of the line, not a policy
  exception.
- **A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact:** none. A sweep for `2026`, `2027`, the
  two callers' names, the item serials, the media serials and the passholder-number prefix returned
  nothing. The only proper nouns are the five mountain names, and they appear solely as the

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**

Every normative atom of the structured source is entailed by the published documents; nothing is
unborne, nothing is borne with changed meaning, and no claim comes from outside the source. All ten
retirements are rendered as retired with their surviving figures and clauses still in force, and
nothing is retired that the source does not declare. All five prerequisite sentences stand verbatim,
in the declared state form, in the hub of the policy they block and in no other policy's document, and
each edge is resolvable at the source's strength from that sentence, the depended-on documents and the
records. All 35 factor ladders are carried in full, tier by tier, threshold by threshold, including
tiers this task never reaches.

No previous revision of this file exists; this is revision 1.

### Policy-side notes (reported, not part of this skill's verdict)

- **P1 — the composition of multiplicative adjustments (consequential).** Three policies say in their
  `baseline.rule` that several shares/uplifts "act on the [base] itself rather than on one another's
  results", while their `compute` expressions form a straight product:
  `rentals_ext_late_handin_fee` (`daily_figure * standing_share * exposure_uplift`),
  `rentals_ext_model_change_fee` (`swap_fee_usd * timing_share * instruction_share * kit_value_uplift`)
  and `rentals_ext_extension_charge` (`extra_day_figure * residence_share * notice_share`). Under a
  product each adjustment *is* worked out on what the previous one left. The same form of words in
  `rentals_ext_counter_settlement` ("none of them acts on another's result") governs three absolute
  amounts, where it genuinely is non-compounding. The KB carries all four sentences verbatim, so the
  bijection holds; the underdetermination is the source's. This is the sole cause of the
  `KB-RUNTIME RED` recorded in `runtime_context/equipment_rental_desk/0.md` and `1.md`.
- **P2 — an unstated window.** `rentals_ext_counter_settlement.compute` reads resort credit as
  `XSUM(... within_months=6 ...)` for both issue and redemption, but neither the policy `rule`, the
  `resort_credit_offset` ladder nor `compute_basis` mentions any window. The KB correctly states no
  window. Immaterial here (the credit was issued 2027-01-12), but a solver reading a pass account
  with older credit would diverge.
- **P3 — unstated intermediate roundings.** `rentals_ext_damage_assessment.compute` rounds at
  `after_school_share` and at `borne_before_ageing`, where the rule prescribes rounding only "at each
  of those steps" (the two set-asides) and at the last step. Immaterial here.
- **P4 — an over-wide base clause.** `rentals_pricing`'s rule sentence "A charge is raised against an
  agreement only while the agreement stands in the reserved, confirmed, picked_up or overdue state"
  is written at full generality, while its eligibility is scoped `applies_to: [rentals_rate_charge]`.
  Read at its face width it would forbid both the damage assessment and the late-hand-in fee that
  task 0 requires on a `returned` agreement — and would make every damage assessment impossible,
  since an assessment is by construction made on handed-in kit. The KB carries the sentence verbatim
  and is right to; the width is the source's. It is resolvable by specificity (the fee policy and the
  damage policy each state their own standing), which is how I resolved it blind.
- **P5 — inconsistent naming of the same ledger family.** The counter baseline names "the hire rate
  and the add-ons raised on it together with the shop fees and the assessments"; the hold-release
  baseline names "the hire rate, the shop fees and the assessments". Both `compute` expressions sum
  every `rentals_rate_charge` row, add-ons included. Faithfully carried on both sides.
- **P6 — day-count wording against day-count binding.** `kit_value_uplift_level` and
  `extension_fee_level` say "the agreement runs for" / "was written for at least the package's
  multi-day threshold in days" while both computes read `rental_days_booked`. Identical on this
  task's agreements; the two counts can differ, and the corpus's own
  `days_charged_for_on_an_agreement_29935120` insists they are "Three counts, not one".
- **P7 — a survivor with nothing to read it.** The retirement of `rentals_swap_and_extension`'s
  extension clause removes the only rule that gated an extension on the package's
  `extension_allowed`; the figure is declared to stand and the schedule still carries it, but no
  surviving rule reads it. Identical in the source and in the KB.

### C. R3-N1 — a document naming an absent authority

The replacement says shop fees and assessments "stand or fall by the standing their own rules fix".
I enumerated the charter's base eligibility entries: there are **11**, and their `applies_to` values
are `rentals_reserve`, `rentals_reserve_load`, `rentals_rate_charge`, `rentals_pickup`,
`rentals_deposit_hold`, `rentals_deposit_release` (×2), `rentals_mark_overdue`, `rentals_fee_charge`,
`rentals_cancel`, `rentals_close`. **None is `rentals_damage_charge`**, and
`rentals_ext_damage_assessment` states no standing of its own. The observation is factual.

**Judgement: a source observation, not a KB defect in this skill's domain.** Three reasons, each
checked rather than assumed:

1. *Bijection.* The sentence is the charter's `replaced_by` verbatim. The corpus invented no standing
   for assessments, added no pointer, and named no rule. Rendering it as the charter states it is the
   correct behaviour, and the instruction the render agent was given was right.
2. *Runtime.* The sentence defers; the documents it defers to impose no bar; the reader therefore
   finds no bar, which is the outcome task 0 needs. The affirmative basis for assessing handed-in kit
   is stated positively elsewhere — `security_hold_and_damage_basis` §2 ("Kit handed in is checked by
   a technician, and what is found is recorded against the serial of the item") and
   `damage_finding_assessment_entry` ("A finding entered when kit was checked back in stands … at nil
   until it is assessed") — so a reader is not left searching for permission. It does not create a
   second reasonable answer, and I re-derived task 0's assessment on a `returned` agreement without
   hesitation.
3. *Not unbounded either.* The corpus is not actually silent about the extreme case the missing
   standing might seem to open: `kit_handin_and_agreement_closure` states "Closing is the last thing
   recorded on the agreement and nothing is added to it afterwards", which bars an assessment on a
   closed agreement. So the practical envelope is closed from another direction.

The residual is honest and worth stating: a sentence that defers to an authority imposing nothing is
weaker than silence would be, because it invites a search that returns nothing. It changes no scored
value, opens no second reading, and belongs to the policy side. Carried forward as note **P8**.

The sentence in `security_hold_waiver_and_replacement_schedule_fa3fcd12.json` now reads:

> "…its waiver, **priced by the day like every other waiver on the line**, stands at **79.00 USD a
> day** against the day-hire packages' **5.00, 7.00, 9.00, 12.00 and 15.00 USD**."

Checked against `variants`: `damage_waiver_daily_usd` is 5.0 / 7.0 / 9.0 / 12.0 / 15.0 for the five
day-hire packages and 79.0 for the Season-Long Lease Package — all six enumerated correctly, with no

**The render agent is right that the old sentence carried two defects, not one, and I found only

So the old sentence also mis-described the schema. Verified directly; the new wording is true on both

### C. Verifying the sweep's coverage, not only its corrections

I did not take the enumeration on report. I ran an independent sweep over all 68 documents with a
deliberately **wider** marker set than the one described (comparatives, superlatives, quantifiers,
pattern words, plus abutment, run, middle, over-again, travel-together and sits-apart forms):

- **363 candidate sentences** matched the marker set (against the 192 reported — a wider net, as
  intended, so that anything their net missed would surface in mine).
- **127 triaged out**: 60 table rows, 10 headings, **57 source-verbatim**.
- **236 kept** for evaluation.

**The triage rule is conservative in the right direction**, which is the point the coordinator asked
me to test. A sentence is dismissed as source-verbatim only when the **whole** sentence, stripped of
its bold lead-in and trailing period, is a substring of the concatenated charter text — every base
rule and eligibility condition, every counting rule, every extended rule and `baseline.rule`, every
`superseded_clause` and `replaced_by`, every `policy_source`, every ladder `when`/`value`/`method` and
every `compute_basis` entry. A sentence that carries a source clause **plus a relational tail** fails
that test and is kept. So the failure mode that matters — a relational claim hiding behind rule
carriage — cannot pass this triage.

Spot-checking the 57 source-verbatim members: every one is a rule, baseline, ladder or
`compute_basis` sentence carried word for word — including the four rewritten composition sentences,
the five prerequisite sentences, "The fee is never more than the package's replacement value", "The
figure the guest bears is never below zero", "Kit already collected is never cancelled", "Two live
agreements for the same rider over overlapping dates are never opened", and the hire-rate order
sentence. Not one is a claim about the shape of a schedule.

The 60 table rows are the cells themselves, every one of which I re-verified against `variants` in
rounds 1 and 2. I checked separately that no table row hides a **derived** column outside that check:
the only derived columns in the corpus are the four "Half of it" columns, "The larger of the two" in
`bundle_share_on_the_hire_rate`, and "Seven days at the multi-day day rate" in
`day_rate_selection_for_longer_agreements` — all asserted below.

Outside the nine facets, I searched every document for prose naming two or more packages, the shape a
cross-package relational claim must take. **Exactly one** exists — "On the Junior Ski & Board Rental a
seventh of the weekly rate of 169.00 USD is 24.14 USD …; on the Performance Ski & Board Rental a
seventh of 419.00 USD is 59.86 USD" — and both figures are correct (169 ÷ 7 = 24.142857 → 24.14;
419 ÷ 7 = 59.857 → 59.86).

**I then wrote 53 assertions evaluating every kept relational claim directly against `variants` and
`parameter_schema`, and ran them: 0 failures.** They cover all five rewritten sentences (20
assertions, including the load-bearing-scoping check and the per-day-key check) and every claim
carried over unchanged: the multi-day gap widening 5→13; the five season lease prices; the grace,
daily-figure and patience runs; the cancellation "larger of the two / exactly twice on four / less
than twice on two" set and the highest-and-lowest sentence; the free-cancellation-equals-hold-hours
claim; the excess step levels; the change allowance widening against change money falling away and
the "two packages including changes are exactly the two showing 0.00"; the extension limits and
Demo's highest fee; the Lease's sole lease exchange and dearest change fee; "item inside the package
⇒ no money against it" across helmet, tune and storage; the storage, delivery and fitting claims; the
signed-release and photo-ID claims; the age-band abutment; the Lease's fitting span and its 60-day
minimum against every day-hire maximum; the 13-year/138-cm hypothetical; the shop-network counts and
"flexible hand-in and a low cross-mountain figure travel together"; the passholder climb and both
bundle figures falling away; the 12.5 per cent figure; the Demo hold-below-replacement point; the
seven-times column; and all four "half of it" columns.

**No further relational defect remains.** The class is clear.

### D. The five rewrites checked for invention

New prose is where invention enters, so each rewrite was checked twice — true of the cells, and
adding no normative claim the charter does not make.

- The **waiver**, **release period**, **late-fee** and **hold-run** rewrites are pure description of
  the tables they sit under. They impose nothing, permit nothing and decide nothing; every figure they
  now name is a cell.
- The **height** sentence needed the closer look, since "a rider of exactly 155 cm falls inside all
  three" reads at first like guidance. It is not. It asserts two facts about the ranges — that Junior's
  maximum and Performance's and Demo's minimum are the same number, and that a rider at that number
  satisfies all three range tests — and stops. It does **not** say which package such a rider is
  fitted in, does not license a choice between them, and does not touch
  `rentals_reservation_terms` clause 2 ("a rider outside the package's fitting range is moved to the
  package that does fit them"), which is carried unchanged in
  `reservation_terms_and_fitting_eligibility`. It is the same species of provable derivation this
  document already made in "A rider of 16 years, 160 cm and 50 kg … falls inside the ranges held
  against the Basic, Sport, Performance and Demo packages", which has stood since round 1. It is also
  not misleading by omission: a 155 cm rider is in fact inside five height bands, and the very next
  sentence says so ("The Basic package begins at 140 cm and the Sport package at 145 cm, both of them
  overlapping the Junior band from below"), so "all three" is plainly scoped to the three bands just
  named and claims no exclusivity. The passage is expressly about height, and the paragraph opens by
  establishing that it is **age** that divides the line cleanly.

**No normative claim was added by any of the five.**

### E. One inaccuracy in the change report

The report states that **no numeral was added to or removed from any document**. My census of every
numeral occurrence across all 68 documents, round 2 against round 3, shows **13 added and 0 removed**:
`18.00`, `28.00`, `38.00`, `52.00`, `68.00` and `10` and `2` in `late_handin_fee_schedule`; `5.00`,
`7.00`, `9.00`, `12.00`, `15.00` in `security_hold_waiver_and_replacement_schedule`; and `155` in
`rider_fitting_range_and_hire_term_schedule`.

This is not a defect — it is the opposite. Every added numeral is a schedule figure now enumerated
inside the rewritten relational sentence, which is precisely what makes the new claims checkable
where the old ones were not, and every one is correct against `variants`. The property that matters
holds exactly: **no figure was changed, and no value appears that the tables do not carry.** But the
claim as written is not true of the corpus, and a reviewer relying on it would draw the wrong
boundary around what the round touched.
